Protests in Philippines seem rly mild rn when you compare to 1980s/2000s

Also a lot of performative middle class disaffected people and leftist college kids (PH leftism is mild and understandable, I don’t despise them like Western woke left yet)

Like I said before, life for the poor has gotten far better. Philippine economy is growing fast, 10% of population is overseas, every slum dweller had the choice that day to protest and earn no money or do food delivery and feed their kids. Plenty of pressure release valves compared to before.

In the 2000s kids starved and begged on the streets while sniffing glue, now with a smartphone and a bike they can earn money, have food to eat, enjoy games/shows and be ultra social.

So this backlash on widespread corruption may be the build-up for massive reform and political disruption in future, but not really a revolutionary moment right now.

data.text:
Hong Kong, southern China hit by powerful Typhoon Ragasa after it batters the Philippines

A huge and deadly typhoon is battering Hong Kong and southern China after lashing the Philippines and Taiwan with destructive winds and torrential rain, putting the region’s megacities on high alert with canceled flights and disruption to schools and businesses.

Tens of millions of people could be impacted by Typhoon Ragasa, which is expected to pass south of major cities Hong Kong, Macau, Shenzhen and Guangzhou, before making landfall again in the west of mainland China’s Guangdong province.

At least 14 people were killed in Taiwan when a barrier lake breached in the eastern county of Hualien, the county’s fire department said on Wednesday morning.
